title: Customer optimization signal taxonomy and routing heuristic
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Define a repeatable, signal-driven taxonomy and routing heuristic for incoming optimization/advisory requests (non-bug) so we can automatically surface the right response lane: self-serve docs/auto-scorer, concierge tuning, or enterprise SLA handoff. Scope covers requests related to batching and caching knobs, quantization profiles, and routing policies. Excludes incident/bug triage and pure feature requests.

Why: We receive high-volume advisory requests that overlap in complexity and customer profile. Current manual triage causes delays and inconsistent outcomes. A signal taxonomy + heuristic will reduce mean time to recommendation, enable predictable SLAs for enterprise customers, and surface signals for productization (self-serve docs, automated suggestions in Console).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented signal taxonomy (signals + weights) covering workload, model, SLAs, cost-sensitivity and security constraints is published in Confluence
A2: A prototype routing heuristic implemented as a decision table and validated on a 30-day sample of historical tickets with >70% alignment to expert triage
A3: Routing lanes defined (Self-serve, Concierge, Enterprise SLA) with clear handoff triggers and SLAs (TTR, response cadence), and the handoff checklist published
A4: Low-risk automation: auto-scorer rules for >40% of incoming advisory requests (non-enterprise) that generate a recommended knob/config with a confidence score and suggested next action
A5: Instrumentation added to intake form to capture required signals and a dashboard (Console) to monitor inflow/lane distribution and time-to-first-recommendation
proposal_summary: We propose a weighted-signal heuristic. Signals: customer_tier (enterprise, paid, free), request_type (batching, caching, quant, routing), observed_latency_cost_delta (low/med/high), reproducibility (has sample workload), security_constraints (PII/regulated), urgency (business-impact), and previous_automations_attempted. Each signal maps to a score; thresholds route to lanes: score >= 80 -> Enterprise SLA (manual engineer-led), 50-79 -> Concierge (timeboxed expert engagement), <50 -> Self-serve (automated docs + auto-scorer). An override flow allows PM/Support to reclassify. Prototype will be a decision table + lightweight evaluator service for validation against historical data.
tradeoffs_decision_log: 2026-02-12: Decided not to fully auto-route enterprise-labeled requests to automation (risk: SLA violation); enterprise always requires human acknowledgment
2026-02-18: Chosen weighted-signal approach over ML classifier for explainability and faster iteration; revisit ML after 3 months of labeled data
2026-02-25: Agreed to include cost-sensitivity bucket (customer-provided) as explicit intake field to improve routing precision
2026-03-03: Opted for conservative auto-scorer coverage target (40%) for initial launch to limit false positives and customer confusion
